caption: Indoor cat, Douliana. Woke up with him inside — no key, no knock, just a tabby on the tiles.
Agios Georgios church. Dragon down, flags up, Apokoronas sun on the paint.
Blue dome, Petres. White walls, dry hill, and a sky that means business.
Dromos into the chamber, Armeni. Stone stairs down, then the dark mouth of the tomb.

Tomb 159, Armeni. Same doorway, three millennia of atmosphere, one very happy explorer.
Melons on the truck, Asimi. The produce aisle got wheels and a Toyota badge.
Fresh figs, Demati. Julia found the island’s best snack aisle growing overhead.
Three figs, Demati. Sunglasses on, harvest in hand, checkout still optional.
Memorial stones at Amiras. A quiet place carrying a hard date: 14 Sep 1943.
Planks into the sea, Myrtos. Greek engineering: two boards and a rope, then stones spelling Kreta.
Sea wall and courtyard, Kales fortress. One visit, two angles, no shortage of stone.
Spinalonga on the horizon. Tomorrow’s island, already posing in the water.
Windmill selfie, Elounda. Bare spokes, full smiles — Greek engineering, selfie edition.
Terracotta dome, Agios Konstantinos & Eleni. Cream walls and a sky doing overtime.
Flag-painted stairs. Smile, hope, love, peace, paradise — all on the way up.
Cocktail Therapy Sessions. Athens 409 km — we’re closer than that.
Sailboats on the table. Toys in front, the real bay behind.
Café on the stairs. Greek engineering: when the street is the seating chart.
Yoga vs Vodka. Same pose, different outcome.
Watermelon crate. 3.50€ — Maria called it years ago.
Almost-kiss at Elounda harbor. Fishing boats, Greek flag, hills across the water.
Μανώλης at the dock. Tall mast, Greek flag on the line.
White skiff in Elounda lagoon. Spinalonga’s walls on the point beyond.
Pebble table by the bay. Little Bear Cabernet and a view that doesn’t rush.
Two Mythos at Alikes Suites. Bay flat, unicorns on the glass.
Handshake dinner at Rakomelo. Octopus on fava, gyro board, Greek salad with the big feta.
Thumbs-up at Rakomelo. Handshake dinner follow-through — net shawl and all.
Twin towers and terracotta roofs in Vryses. The church keeps time whether anyone asks.
Vryses: terraced water, a parliament of white ducks, Coca-Cola umbrellas. Soft landing after the hills.
Trophy board from Alikampos. Whatever was on it, the smile says it landed.
Looking out the stone doorway into the light. Alikampos does exits well.
Hands in the grapes, hillside dry as toast. Alikampos harvest energy.
Dark grapes with the bloom still on. Alikampos vines doing September work.
Stone arch, wooden door, Alikampos. The wall has better bones than most hotels.
Barrel table under a big tree in Alikampos. Shade that earns its keep.
Turquoise canal, pedalos lined up like they have plans. Georgioupolis after lunch.
Table flowers, umbrella pole, and that little chapel on the rocks. Georgioupolis view for free.
Jumbo shrimp on a fish-shaped plate. The sea was right there. So was the beer.
Skewer, peppers, a mountain of fries. Georgioupolis does lunch properly.
Georgioupolis jetty: white chapel, Greek flag, a skinny beacon that means business.
Likotinarea in black and white. Alpha, Omega, one bell. The chapel doesn’t need color.
Two Mythos, sea behind the foam. Georgioupolis lunch hours.
Corner of Kefalas. Stone house, iron balcony, mountains peeking like they own the street.
Stone flag and a roadside shrine for Vaggelis Dermitsis. Kefalas remembers in rock.
Rock ledge at Kefalas. Book open, ladder in, water so clear you can read the bottom.
Kefalas bay from above. Turquoise shallows, navy deep, three white cats parked like they pay marina rent.
Dry-docked in Georgioupolis, paint hanging off, red stripes still on. This hull is out of the water and still the thirstiest thing on the beach.
Caught in the act. Douliana’s cat burglar, using the front door like they pay rent.
Best dessert in Crete isn’t baklava. It’s watermelon, melon, and a raki you didn’t order. Arkadi, Georgioupolis.
Cold melon after a long Apokoronas loop. Douliana knows how to end a day.
The lamp comes on and Douliana leans a little. Village corners do that at dusk.
Village HR. A Douliana cat on the stone wall, reviewing our papers.
Boonville hat, Douliana pool. Home came with us; the water is new.
Roadside devotion in Xirosterni: Agios Fanourios in stacked stone, flags, and “love one another.”
A stone mill on the Kalyves–Kefalas road, roof long gone, sky doing the rest. Drapanos.
Taverna Zorbas, Kokkino Chorio. White chairs, a eucalyptus, and a table that would have kept us.
Greek junkfood, and we meant it. Ham-and-pepper pizza at Tsunami after the Almyrida swim.
Two Mythos under the thatch. Almyrida, Tsunami, DDIC hours.
Pocket chapel, a rock full of white fans, village stacked behind. Almyrida heat protocol.
Rocks in water that looks edited. Almyrida from the swim.
Two chairs under a thatch umbrella, a still bay, white houses climbing the hill. One of those would be a good contender for an investment. DDIC (Day Drinking In Crete) house? Who’s in?
Raki, guns, and Crete. A great combo.
On raki at Ηλιοστάσι. Bottle in one hand, shot in the other.
Mixed grill at Ηλιοστάσι (Heliostasi) — sausage, chops, herbed fries. Delicious. The huge Cretan salad still hanging around.
Cretan salad the size of a small island at Ηλιοστάσι, creamy tzatziki crowding the plate.
Last light over Douliana. Us, the pool, and the hills catching fire.
Douliana pool, two floaties, mountains for a backsplash.
Corner fireplace, wicker chairs, village light through the sheers.
Raki glasses on the yellow cloth. Home for a minute.
Pulled over for the gulf. Town, sea, and that end-of-drive grin.
Sky-blue church, clock in the tower, hibiscus on the fence. Pulled over because Crete was showing off.
Manousakis through a stone door in white flowers. Bottles in the shade, heat outside.
Barrels down a vaulted aisle. Cool, dark, and a little cinematic.
Green olives still deciding. Spiderweb included, no extra charge.
A prickly pear the size of a small car. Fruit everywhere.
Hatzimichalis Giannaris in vraka, keeping watch over the village.
Red dome, white village, mountains stacked behind. Lakkoi from the road.
Three fighters stacked like a toast. Lakkoi does not do small monuments.
White houses on a green hill. The mountains doing the rest.
A gorge that keeps going. Crete showing off its bones.
Local committee inspecting the asphalt. We waited.
Ridge selfie — hills, a wink of sea, and us looking suspiciously pleased.
Yellow chapel, yellow phone booth. Even the mountains coordinate.
Sheep parked in the olive shade. Peak Cretan traffic.
Watermelon and something sweet with raki. Caravella’s idea of a soft landing.
Caravella after the heat broke — table on the rocks, mountains across the water.
Two gin and tonics at Livikon Day to Night. Lemon, peppercorns, sea, and those mountains doing their thing.
Caravella, Paleochora. Grilled calamari, souvlaki and fries, and the whole steam-table parade — last night’s dinner did not play small.
A silver cloud over the pebbles. Gialiskari underwater is basically a fish freeway.
Us at Gialiskari Beach. Clear water, pebble shore, and that mid-afternoon grin.
Waist-deep at Gialiskari. Pebbles underfoot, hillside behind, nowhere else to be.
Threading the rocks toward Gialiskari. The kind of road that makes you slow down just to stare.
Dirt road, cliff on the left, sea on the right. Gialiskari is somewhere past that white car.
White hood, rock shadows, and a road that keeps inventing new corners.
Mountain hairpins and a first wink of sea. Crete does the long way on purpose.
Julia in the shallows at Elafonissi. Smile, sunglasses, and water so clear the sand looks like a filter.
Saltwater kiss at Elafonissi. Clear enough to see freckles, and somehow still not clear enough to explain how good this felt.
One tiny neighbor. Sand ripples, turquoise glass, and a little silver streak that owns the whole frame.
Underwater selfie, masks on, thumbs up. Θάλασσα — the whole point of the day.
Knee-deep in glass. Elafonissi does that thing where the water looks fake and you keep checking if you’re still awake.
Dinner in the courtyard after dark. Soft lights, stone walls, and that same pinch-me feeling: are we still in the movie?
Meats, cheeses, grapes — the whole board. Romeiko Wine & Deli, dinner done right.
Two reds at Romeiko Wine & Deli. First sip, and the village feels even more like a set we somehow wandered onto.
Us on the pebble beach at dusk. The light is unfairly good — like someone paid for this sky.
A Crete flag and a tiny chapel on the rocks at dusk. We keep waiting for the director to yell cut.
Somebody's scooter, parked like it belongs in a travel poster. Green courtyard, quiet street, Hollywood-village energy.
Blue tables by the water and a ferry parked like an extra. Paleochora at golden hour — half fishing village, half movie set.
Paleochora. The view from our balcony.
The church next to I Platia in Kandanos.
Spicy meatballs at I Platia in Kandanos. Red sauce, a pile of fries. The best.
After lunch at I Platia. Cinnamon-dusted sweet and a little raki.
Stones stacked on the sand. Beach near Sunny Bay, Kissamos.
The Manassa wreck. North coast, Kissamos Bay.
Us on the north coast.
Roadside shrines on the north coast.
Two frappés by the harbour. Yia mas.
It's not Greece without a protest.
Full moon last night. Harbour dark, Chania lit up under it.
Stumbled into the Chania film festival. Old projector, good times.
Us at TAMAM, old-town alley. Excellent food.
Lamb kabobs, pita, a pile of fries. Excellent.
Wine-braised octopus, fries on the side. Excellent.
Dakos and fava, together with the wine. Excellent.
More frappés by the harbour. Two straws, one view.
Best gyros in town, or a close second. We're not arguing with the pita.
The spit at Το Σουβλάκι Όπως Παλιά. This is the one.
Julia at Saturday market. Grapes by the crate.
Potatoes, sixty cents.
August tomatoes. Saturday market, piled high.
Street grill at Saturday market. Smoke and a euro thirty a skewer.
Fort ruins after dark. Stones, empty windows, the whole wall lit.
The Botanist. Great cocktails. We'll be back.
Aged Long Island, skip the Coke. The Botanist.
Whole fish off the grill. Tomato, onion, herbs — the plate is the whole point.
Dakos before the fish. Barley rusks, tomato, onion, cucumber, a pile of cheese.
From the boat. Turquoise water and cliffs dropping in.
Stopped the boat. A dip in the Mediterranean.

Carbonana Gate, Elounda. Cobblestones, a crooked tree, and us in matching sunglasses.
Spinalonga approach. Grinning on deck with the fortress coming into view.
Fortress passage. Julia takes the narrow route through the old stone.
Stone oven. A built-in kitchen with centuries of heat still in the walls.
Fortress chapel. Icons, chandelier, and a quiet pocket inside the stone.
Old window. Two travelers framed by Cretan light.
Ruined windows. The roof is gone; the sky moved in.
Bay arch. The fortress opens straight onto blue water.
Ruined doorway. An olive tree has claimed the courtyard.
Fortress steps. Upward, with the bay waiting between the stones.
Sea-facing embrasure. A rectangle of blue cuts through the fortress wall.
Bay view. The fortress finally gives the sea the whole frame.
Fortress ruins. A little archaeology, a lot of shameless posing.
Fortress arch. Stone overhead, blue bay beyond.
Fortress ridge. Ruins above, boats below, Cretan afternoon sorted.
Boats in the bay. Small wakes, big Spinalonga backdrop.
Fortress shade. A tree, a bench, and a view worth stopping for.
Stone wall by the bay. Sun-warmed masonry, blue water, no hurry.
Sea wall. The fortress meets the water in full afternoon light.
Fortress tunnel. Down the dark passage toward a brighter blue.
Tunnel selfie. Ordinary doorways never stood a chance.
Tunnel window. Sea and sky at the end of the passage.
Retired fishing boat. Sea view, string lights, and one last shift as décor.
Turquoise cove. Jagged rocks, a stone wall, and water too clear to fake.
Ancient olive tree. Daniel found the village’s best shade and claimed the frame.
Stone path to the sea. Lunch is hiding under the tree, just ahead.
Meatballs and pita. Cold beer, lemony drink, perfect timing.
Two caiques at the rocks. Greek flag up, turquoise water doing the rest.
Giorgos Giavannis sign. Pufferfish, shells, and a tree with a full personality.
Giant shell basin. A seaside garden detail that refuses to be subtle.
Beach selfie. Turquoise water, tamarisk shade, and nowhere else to be.
Stone bridge and fishing boats. Turquoise water slips under the old crossing.
Frozen red cocktails. Two straws, one bright-blue bay, zero complaints.
Ancient olive tree at night. The dinner garden got its own spotlight.
Four-frame feast. Crispy bites, meatballs, rosy roast, and fish — the kitchen did not believe in small plates.
Octopus tart. Capers, herbs, golden crust — Cretan coast energy in one beautiful bite.
Fresh-baked bread and hummus. Grain, wheat, and the table already making its case.
Issorropia Cabernet. Two glasses, one bottle, evening soundtrack.
Agios Konstantinos & Eleni at night. Clock tower, palms, dome, and a square lit for the occasion.
FOOD DRINK under the church dome. Full tables, bright sign, Elounda night.
Roadside chapel among the olives. A tiny roof, a red dome, and Crete doing quiet details.
Colourful chairs outside Mamma Mio! Looks fun—and the mountain road agrees.
Old windmill. Even the dry hillside brought a little motion to the stop.
Ancient rooms in the ruins. Malia’s hillside view makes the old floor plan feel surprisingly open.
Ancient jar, two grins. Malia came with its own giant souvenir.
A giant Minoan storage jar. One amphora, several thousand years of attitude.
Minoan rooms under the canopy. The oldest floor plan still has excellent bones.
A wooden bridge over the ruins. Ancient archaeology, modern balance beam.
Ancient stone rooms. History in warm earth tones, with the roof kept modern.
Rooms and thresholds in the ruins. The past left a whole neighborhood to wander through.
Three chairs by the sea. Shade, salt air, and a table waiting for absolutely nothing.
New Airbnb kitchen. First look at the Heraklion apartment—and yes, the bright blue cabinets have already clocked in.
Hibiscus on the sidewalk. Heraklion’s old-town lanes know how to add color to a walk.
Stone fountain in the square. Heraklion left the shade, carved details, and a little water running.
Lion fountain. The old square is still doing excellent people-watching, even when the lions are stone.
Two frappés. A cold coffee break with the table doing the thinking.
A whole building in color. Heraklion street art turned balconies into a comic-book block.
Pizza night. Great pizza, good wine, and absolutely no leftovers energy.
Tiramisu. Delicious enough to finish the meal—and on the house because we were family (same last name).
Night-lit neoclassical façade. Heraklion after dark has more details than the daytime itinerary.
Stained-glass windows and palms. Agios Titos keeps a quiet Heraklion night framed in color.
Fortress on the water. Heraklion’s Koules lit up and keeping watch.
7276th Communications Squadron wall. Dad was stationed here when he met Mom — base closed, story still open.
Old fire department, Iraklion Air Station. Quiet now — this is where Dad was stationed when he met Mom.
Station gatehouse, Gournes. One small Crete stop with a very big family story.
Four lions selfie. Us in the square — Morosini’s lions doing the serious work behind us.
Bronze dolphins leaping by the marina. Racing the Koules fortress for first splash.
Selfie under the Lion of St. Mark. Koules still on guard duty — and so are the sunglasses.
Vaulted stone halls and studded doors. Half expecting a Venetian captain to walk through.
Heavy wooden door, diamond iron studs, tiny padlock. Whatever’s behind it is staying put.
A floor full of ancient amphorae. Someone’s olive-oil pantry got seriously out of hand.
Weathered battlements and a pale blue sky. Fortress shade never goes out of style.
Harbor selfie from the Koules walls. Turquoise water, sailboats, and zero complaints.
Freddo espresso. The new Greek coffee — frothy, iced, and walk-ready.
Pork souvlaki, crispy potatoes, and cold tzatziki. The plate that ends the “what’s for lunch” debate.
Empty green tables and seaside murals in a quiet alley. Saving seats for the evening rush.
Twin towers and red domes of Agios Minas. Reaching straight into that Cretan blue.
St. Titus under a perfect blue sky. Dome, plaza, and a little divine calm mid-walk.
Ornate facade of St. Titus — belfry, oculus, open door. History with the door ajar.
Agios Minas behind the construction fence. Even mid-facelift, that cathedral still owns the skyline.
Vintage motorcycle parked on Archanon Street. Looks ready for one more Cretan lap.
Two tiny soups in crystal glasses — cream, crumb, and a green leaf. Peskesi saying hello before the real plates arrive.
Douloufakis Sangiovese–Cabernet. One bottle, one glass, and Peskesi’s placemat already making the case.
Four-frame feast at Peskesi. Onion-topped meat on flatbread, beans in olive oil, snails with summer veg, and slow-roasted pork with bright purées.
Semolina halva with cinnamon and nuts. Soft landing after a Cretan feast.
Pizza and tiramisu. Great pie, house dessert — same last name privilege.
